newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares power higher on ADRs, Fed decision.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares power higher on ADRs, Fed decision.

text.p: Leading Russian shares stormed to new highs in early morning trade on Thursday on the back of high demand for American Depositary Receipts and in the wake of the U.S. Fed's decision not to raise interest rates, traders said.
They saw the uptrend continuing in the short term.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at a record 449.61 after Wednesday's record 447.94 closing.
"The race continues -- for now everything is growing, mainly blue chips, and people have even become distracted from regional telecoms," said Troika Dialog sales manager German Zvezdin.
He added that closing ADR prices in New York presaged Thursday's surge on local underlying shares in Moscow.
"It's completely obvious that people have money," he said.
"Judging by the growth of funds which deal with Russia there's no problem getting the money to put into Russia -- indeed, there is a constant influx of capital which has to be placed."

Global Depositary Receipts on national electricity company UES traded at around $40 on Thursday, a Bank of New York spokesman said, while oil company LUKoil American Depositary Receipts closed up $5.00 at $86.00 on Wednesday.
Local shares in UES shot up over 10 percent in the first half hour of trade to $0.4650 after closing on Wednesday at $0.4055 but fell back at 0945 GMT to $0.4420.
LUKoil rose to $21.500 from $21.100 and regional utility Mosenergo ticked up to $1.495 from $1.450 and international long-distance provider Rostelekom firmed to $4.80 from $4.45.
Creditanstalt Grant senior trader Andrei Galperin said the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision on Wednesday not to raise interest rates had helped the optimistic mood on the market.

Zvezdin said an auction now in progress of a 25 percent plus one share stake in state telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, which owns 38 percent of Rostelekom, was helping to excite interest in the long-distance carrier.
